title: "Train/Test Split"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This example demonstrates stratified train/test splitting using the `aoclda` package.

```{r library}
library(aoclda)
```

## Define Data

```{r data}
X <- matrix(
   c(
      -2.0, 3.1, 5.5, 0.0, 1.1, -3.3, 2.2, 4.4, -1.1, 3.3,
      4.2, -1.2, 2.3, -4.4, 3.3, 0.0, -2.2, 1.1, 5.5, -3.3,
      1.5, 0.0, -3.3, 2.2, -1.1, 4.4, 3.3, -0.5, 0.0, 1.1
   ),
   nrow = 10, ncol = 3
)

y <- matrix(
   c(
      -2.5, 3.7, -1.1, 4.4, -3.3, 2.2, -4.8, 1.5, 0.0, -6.6,
      3.5, -4.7, 2.1, -5.4, 4.3, -3.2, 5.8, -2.5, 1.0, 7.6
   ),
   nrow = 10, ncol = 2
)

classes <- c(2, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1)
```

## Split

```{r split}
result <- train_test_split(X, y,
   test_size = 0.4, train_size = 0.6,
   seed = 42, shuffle = TRUE, stratify = classes
)
X_train <- result[[1]]
X_test <- result[[2]]
y_train <- result[[3]]
y_test <- result[[4]]
```

## Results

```{r results}
cat("X_train:\n")
print(X_train)

cat("\nX_test:\n")
print(X_test)

cat("\ny_train:\n")
print(y_train)

cat("\ny_test:\n")
print(y_test)
```
